name: CycleWire, inline
summary: The CycleWire app with the core inlined in the page: CycleWire starts while the page is still parsing, and each action's code loads as one module when someone reaches for it.

variant.differs: The core is the classic-script build inlined in <head>, which starts from a JSON block that maps actions to URLs, instead of a module loaded with the page; the actions are one module each (esbuild) instead of Vite chunks. It tests the performance guide's advice to inline the core for the fastest activation.

idioms.choice: The core is the classic-script build, inlined in <head> after a <script type="application/json" data-cyclewire> block that maps each action to its module's URL, as the performance guide suggests for the fastest activation: it starts while the page is still parsing, with no request of its own.
Actions are registered by URL from the JSON block, the way a page without a bundler registers them.
esbuild builds each action into one module with what it imports bundled in, so loading an action is one request. Modules that two actions include, such as cyclewire/signals, keep one state per page.

Add to cart, the action most visitors use first, is preloaded with the page: the server writes <link rel="modulepreload"> for its chunk and the chunks it imports, from Vite's manifest, so a tap on it right after the page appears waits only for the server. Everything else loads on intent, the default, and on touch screens also once the page is idle.
The cart header is bound to a store the server serializes (cw-store, cw-bind); cyclewire/signals arrives with the cart action.
The quick view fetches JSON and renders it with cyclewire/dom, which arrives with that action.

The prefetch plugin is a module that registers with the running CycleWire through CycleWire.use(): the quick view link names its data with cw-prefetch, fetched on intent next to the action's code, and ctx.fetch() takes the response. A quick view before that module runs asks the server itself.
